summary: On paper Cincinnati has the edge (Cincinnati ranks 2nd of 32 in EPA per dropback, +0.29), one of its biggest strengths this season), while Carolina's best counter is to tackle in space (Carolina's defense ranks 1st of 32 in YAC over expected per catch, -0.9 yds allowed), one of its biggest strengths this season). Under center, Joe Burrow ranks 1st of 31 in EPA per dropback and Bryce Young ranks 19th; x-factor: Ja'Marr Chase gets 29% of Cincinnati's targets and 40% of its air yards, and his WOPR (0.69) ranks 10th of 121. Carolina's pass defense ranks 23rd. The model favors Cincinnati at 66%, mostly on passing matchup (3.2 pts) and starting QB (2.9 pts).

CIN.detail: Cincinnati ranks 2nd of 32 in EPA per dropback (+0.29), one of its biggest strengths this season.
Cincinnati ranks 2nd in red-zone TD rate (66%). Carolina's defense ranks 31st (67% allowed).
Cincinnati's defense ranks 23rd in broken tackles per touch (11.2% missed). Carolina ranks 5th (6.3%).

CAR.detail: Carolina's defense ranks 1st of 32 in YAC over expected per catch (-0.9 yds allowed), one of its biggest strengths this season.
Carolina ranks 31st in pressure rate (24%). Cincinnati's defense ranks 17th (22% generated).
Carolina's defense ranks 4th in explosive play rate (7.6% allowed). Cincinnati ranks 12th (9.2%).
